output.brief: Resignations are concentrated in one place: 8 of the 11 associates on Kestrel have left, against 1 of the 13 who were never on it. The firm-wide hours increase and general market mobility don't explain a gap like that, since other groups are stable. Every Kestrel associate reported to Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no one else. So the records can't separate the heavy document-review workload from his supervision style. Survey comments point at both: weekend work, and late-night corrections copied to the whole team. Pay is mentioned, but the one-in-thirteen rate among non-Kestrel associates doesn't fit a pay-driven story. The exit forms are weak evidence: they were completed with HR, leavers were told the group head might see them, and none records the matter or partner. I'm fairly sure the problem is Kestrel-specific. I'm unsure whether workload or supervision is the main driver. Don't announce the retention payment or close the review. Commission the confidential external interviews, which cost about £9k and take three weeks. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Decide on a supervision change or contract reviewers once the interviews are back. Kestrel's heavy phase ends in December, so the timing is tight.
